title: Miles Davis and Bitches Brew
summary: Maxwell says Miles considered the record a put-on.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: I saw him once on the Dick Cavett Show, that whole rock group, Miles. Just ridiculous.
Well, you know, he made that record, Bitch's Brew, I think it was called, a real strange record. And he was telling everybody that was a put-on record. I don't think we talked about that before.
It was sort of a put-on, you know. Put-on for the rock groups and everything. What the hell, he's got this contract with Columbia and I guess he wasn't selling

too good, he was going to make a commercial record to sell, or something. It was a b.s. kind of record. And he got all these heavy reviews, the intellectuals got ahold of it. "The significance of the angry Negro in modern society." And I guess he sat down and said, goddamn, you know, I guess that's what I was doing.
Maybe I didn't know it. So he started to believe it himself and put out a couple more.
It's funny what a writer can put down about you, and you start believing it.
More musicians and artists have been killed like that.

They do that to their own selves, too, the writers. I read some novelist or something, read a review of his book, you know, what the significance of his book was. "Gee," he said, "Did I say all that? I was just trying to tell a story. I didn't know I had all that meaning in there." He was just trying to tell a good detective story, or something.
Yeah, make a big scene out of it.

Well, it's like Dizzy said, Miles, you know, that story about Bitch's Brew. He said, are you going to play that tonight? "Yeah." He said, "Why?" He said, "Because I'm going to be in the front row with a tape recorder and after there's going to be questions."

Miles said, 'what do you mean, man? And Diz said, 'what the hell is that?' He said, 'that's jazz.' He said, 'no, I thought jazz was something that made you wave your hands, wiggle your ass and holler, and that don't do it.'
